question: The concept of Uniform Civil Code is a part of which category of principles in the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles of State Policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The concept of the **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)** is enshrined in Article 44 of the Indian Constitution under the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**.
 
• Article 44 directs the State to strive to secure a UCC for all citizens throughout the territory of India to ensure **uniformity in personal laws**.
 
• The UCC aims to replace personal laws based on the scriptures and customs of each major religious community in India with a common set governing every citizen.
 
• The DPSPs, including the provision for UCC, are **non-justiciable in nature**, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts but aim to guide the State in policymaking.
 
• The objective of the UCC is to promote **national integration and gender equality** by ensuring that personal laws do not discriminate based on religion or gender.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12-35) and are enforceable by the courts.
 
• They guarantee individual rights such as the right to equality, freedom, and protection against exploitation, and ensure cultural and educational rights for minorities.
 
• Although Fundamental Rights are enforceable, the Uniform Civil Code is not part of this category as it is non-justiciable and falls under DPSPs.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• Fundamental Duties are incorporated in Part IV-A (Article 51A) of the Constitution and were added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
 
• They outline the moral obligations of citizens, such as respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, safeguarding public property, and protecting the environment.
 
• The UCC is not part of Fundamental Duties as it pertains to State policy and not individual duties.
 
 
 
• **Preamble Objectives**
 
 
• The Preamble serves as the introduction to the Constitution, outlining the guiding principles and objectives of the Indian State such as justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• While the Preamble reflects the ideals of the Constitution, it is not enforceable and does not directly mention the UCC.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**
 
 
• DPSPs are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution and are aimed at achieving socio-economic justice and welfare.
 
• These principles guide the State in formulating policies that ensure the socio-economic and political welfare of the citizens.
 
• While not enforceable, they are fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to create a welfare state.
